portal_hypertension.abstract: A previously well man in his 20s presented with fever, cough, new-onset jaundice and a right-sided pleural effusion. Initial investigations demonstrated marked hepatic synthetic dysfunction. Subsequent imaging demonstrated cirrhotic liver morphology with splenomegaly and ascites. Additional findings of gallbladder wall oedema and focal colonic wall thickening broadened the differentials but following specialist radiology review, these abnormalities were recognised as manifestations of portal hypertension rather than separate disease processes.Further investigations confirmed Wilson's disease including Kayser-Fleischer rings, low serum caeruloplasmin, MRI brain consistent with Wilson's diseas...

To investigate the effect of hypoxia-induced MAMs formation on gastric mucosal lesions in patients with severe hepatic disorders. Liver cirrhosis (LC) and hepatic failure (HF) were selected as representative severe hepatic diseases, and gastric mucosal tissues were collected.
